subject: community-medicine
title: Neonatal, infant and under-five health: key indicators and programmes

steps.tx: The **infant mortality rate** is the number of deaths under one year of age in a year per 1000 live births in the same year. The **neonatal mortality rate** counts deaths within the first 28 days of life per 1000 live births. The **perinatal mortality rate** covers late stillbirths of 28 weeks or more plus early neonatal deaths in the first week, per 1000 live births. Know the denominator for each: live births for the infant and neonatal rates, and live births again for perinatal in standard Indian teaching.
steps.say: The infant mortality rate counts deaths under one year per 1000 live births in the same year. The neonatal mortality rate counts deaths within the first 28 days per 1000 live births. The perinatal mortality rate covers late stillbirths of 28 weeks or more plus early neonatal deaths in the first week, expressed per 1000 live births. Remember the denominator is live births for all three.

rows: Late stillbirths plus early neonatal deaths

steps.tx: The **under five mortality rate** counts deaths under five years per 1000 live births and is the basic measure of child survival. The **child survival index** is derived by subtracting the under five mortality rate from 1000 and dividing by 10 to get a percentage. Under five mortality is a key indicator used in the child survival index. Infant and child survival are closely linked to maternal and neonatal care.
steps.say: The under five mortality rate counts deaths under five years per 1000 live births and is the basic measure of child survival. The child survival index is found by subtracting the under five mortality rate from 1000 and dividing the result by 10, giving a percentage of children who survive to age five.

steps.tx: **Kangaroo mother care** involves skin to skin contact, exclusive breast feeding and early discharge with follow up. Exclusive breast feeding means giving only breast milk for the first six months, with no water. Breast feeding should start as early as possible after birth, and continued up to two years. IMNCI uses colour coding: green means home care, yellow means outpatient care with local treatment, and pink means outpatient pre referral treatment.
steps.say: Kangaroo mother care involves skin to skin contact, exclusive breast feeding and early discharge with follow up. Exclusive breast feeding means only breast milk for the first six months, with no water. Breastfeeding should start as early as possible and continue up to two years. Under IMNCI, green means home care, yellow means outpatient treatment, and pink means pre referral treatment.

steps.tx: An **under five clinic** provides preventive, promotive, curative and referral services in one place. Weight is recorded monthly in the first year, every two months in the second year and every three months thereafter up to five to six years. Plotting weight on a **growth chart** helps detect early growth failure. Maternal factors such as anaemia, age under 18 or over 35, a last birth less than two years earlier, and more than four previous children harm child health, while haemoglobin of 12 g/dL is normal in India.
steps.say: An under five clinic provides preventive, promotive, curative and referral services in one place. Weight is recorded monthly in the first year, every two months in the second year and every three months after that up to five to six years. Plotting weight on a growth chart helps detect early growth failure. A haemoglobin of 12 grams per decilitre is normal in Indian women.
